report.summary: Alert EVAL-05 on host WS-SAL-03 shows PowerShell executing a script from the user's Temp folder with an execution policy bypass, establishing dual persistence mechanisms via a scheduled task and a registry Run key pointing to C:\Users\Public\syshelper.exe. Threat intelligence correlates syshelper.exe with past true-positive alerts.

claims.text: The alerting tool EDR reported a new scheduled task and Run key pointing to a public folder due to persistence-related changes made by a PowerShell process.
PowerShell executed a script from the user's Temp folder using an execution policy bypass.
A scheduled task named OneDriveSync was created to execute C:\Users\Public\syshelper.exe at logon.
A registry Run key was added containing a value string pointing to C:\Users\Public\syshelper.exe.
Threat intelligence confirms that syshelper.exe was previously seen in a past true positive alert involving scheduled task creation.

recommended_next_steps: Isolate host WS-SAL-03 from the network to prevent further persistence activity or lateral movement.
Terminate active malicious processes associated with syshelper.exe and PowerShell execution if still running.
Remove the unauthorized scheduled task OneDriveSync and clean up the malicious registry Run key.
Collect and analyze the script C:\Users\tnguyen\AppData\Local\Temp\setup.ps1 and the binary C:\Users\Public\syshelper.exe for further forensic evaluation.
Hunt across the enterprise for other hosts executing setup.ps1 or referencing syshelper.exe.
